Published online:
    September 1, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary focus: USA, Japan); secondary: Australia, New Zealand, Europe

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    The yen is holding near 160/USD amid rising BOJ rate hike expectations (73% probability for September), supported by pressure from US Treasury Secretary Bessent. Simultaneously, the USD faces headwinds despite Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks stoking Fed hike bets (65% probability for September, up from 41% a week prior). Rising oil prices (Brent >$91) from renewed Gulf/Iran conflict are driving a bond selloff, pushing 10Y Treasury yields to their highest since January 2025 and 10Y JGB yields to 3% for the first time in 30 years. Markets are navigating dual central bank tightening risk (Fed + BOJ) against a geopolitical inflation backdrop.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (The article is co-centered on USD dynamics, Fed rate hike expectations, and rising Treasury yields — these are core threads throughout)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 80 (Warsh's hawkish tone, CME FedWatch pricing, and rising yields all point strongly toward hike expectations)
Probability of increase: 65%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 15 (Holding is implicitly the baseline being challenged, but not the article's thrust)
Probability of holding: 35%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (No discussion of cuts whatsoever)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 65 (Meaningfully more hawkish than before — Warsh's Jackson Hole debut signaled tightening bias, Fed hike odds jumped sharply from 41% to 65% in one week, and rising oil/yields reinforce the inflationary pressure narrative; partially offset by USD underperformance suggesting market skepticism about Fed credibility restoration)
